role: reader on r/WritingPrompts who has just finished a fellow redditor's short fiction response and is writing a reply with feedback on the writer's craft, choices, and execution
input_unit: reader-feedback comment (the [THIS reply] block, shown in the context of the prompt, the story it responds to, and any earlier replies in the chain)
target: the short fiction the redditor wrote in response to the prompt (the STORY block, possibly continued across the author's later self-replies)
inline_evidence_example: the phrase "the pacing in the middle felt slow — too much exposition before the inciting moment" is a complaint that evidences a 'pacing balance between exposition and scene' norm without naming it; the phrase "love how the reveal lands through the brother's POV instead of just narrating it" is praise that evidences a 'show-don't-tell via POV choice' norm; the phrase "the dialogue tag on this line is missing a comma which makes the speaker ambiguous" is a complaint that evidences a 'dialogue punctuation correctness' norm
polarity_hint: r/WritingPrompts feedback skews encouraging — praise and effusive openers ('wow!', 'loved this!', 'great writing') are the rule, substantive critique is the exception. Extract a signal ONLY when the commenter ties a quality judgment to a specific craft element: voice, pacing, dialogue, characterisation, imagery, prose register, world-building, structure, POV, the use of a particular literary device, or a concrete line/passage they quote with `>` blockquotes. Bare-affect reactions ('wow', 'amazing', 'loved this', 'thank you for writing', 'I cried', 'made my day') are NOT signals — skip them. Reactions to the story's content as content ('I love that the villain wins', 'I want a sequel', 'who is the woman in the painting?') are NOT craft signals unless tied to a craft observation. Joke replies, banter, off-topic riffs, and meta-discussions about other prompts also yield ZERO passages. The story author's own continuation replies in the chain are CONTEXT, not feedback — only the [THIS reply] block is the unit to extract from. Most leaf comments here will yield 0-2 substantive signals; very dense workshop-style critiques can yield 5-10.
